title: SI — One input. Every language.
description: Meet SI, an open-source macOS input method. Choose your languages once, see their candidates together, and keep your original input available. Development preview.
eyebrow: An open-source input method for macOS
intro: Your thoughts don’t switch modes. Your input method shouldn’t have to, either. Choose your languages once. Let their candidates meet.
requirement: macOS 14+ · Apple Silicon / Intel · Free & open source
demoNote: An illustrated demo using SI’s example vocabulary. Each word or phrase is committed separately.
windowSubtitle: Made for more than one language.
demoAccessible: With Chinese and English enabled together, typing shi offers Chinese candidates such as 是 and English completions such as ship. The original shi remains available. Then nihao is committed as 你好, followed by world as world, without changing language modes.
scene1Body: Type shi. Chinese matches, English completions, and your original input share the same list.
scene2Body: Type nihao, then select 你好. Commit the phrase and keep your train of thought.
scene3Body: Type world next. Commit it in English, using the very same input source.
aboutTitle:
A small idea,
a little more flow.
feature1Body: Enable English and Simplified Chinese in Settings. SI asks both for candidates as you type, keeping ambiguous matches available.
feature2Body: Names, code, or something new. Your exact original input is always an explicit option, even when no language matches.
feature3Body: Candidate processing happens on your Mac. No cloud inference, analytics, or keystroke logging.
previewLabel: A work in progress, in the open.
previewBody: SI is a development preview. Production-level vocabulary coverage, sentence-level ranking, and broad app compatibility are still work in progress.
downloadEyebrow: For the curious. For the builders.
downloadBody: Download the developer preview, explore the code, or help shape what comes next.
releaseStatus: Choose the version for your Mac’s chip. Open the DMG, then run Install SI.pkg. Save your work before the installer’s final Log Out step, then log back in and add SI under English in Keyboard settings.
arm64SourceLabel: Source for the Apple Silicon version
